content.text:
Map each node in every diagram on the provided canvas to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change any diagram’s text or the canvas layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (terminal):
Map d5 all nodes. Read numbered source ranges, return JSON partial mappings.

    56	/// A single node within the PageList linked list.
    57	///
    58	/// This isn't pub because you can access the type via List.Node.
    59	const Node = struct {
    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   116	    pub inline fn pageIfResident(self: *Node) ?*Page {
   117	        return switch (self.data) {
   118	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   119	            .compressed => null,
   120	        };
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    /// Read-only page with full memory access that doesn't change
   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains
   125	    /// compressed.
   126	    ///
   127	    /// Resident pages are borrowed directly. So they're basically free.
   128	    ///
   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page
   130	    /// by the caller so callers can inspect their contents. Because resident
   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},
   152	                // The clone buffer came from the caller's allocator rather
   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.
   154	                .owned => |*owned| owned.alloc.free(owned.page.memory),
   155	            }
   156	            self.* = undefined;
   157	        }
   158	    };
   159	
   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(
   169	        self: *const Node,
   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {
   175	                const memory = try alloc.alignedAlloc(
   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );
   180	
   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {
   182	                    // The encoded data was produced by our codec and remains
   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.
   185	                    switch (err) {
   186	                        error.TruncatedInput,
   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
   195	                    @panic("failed to clone compressed terminal page");
   196	                };
   197	
   198	                break :owned .{ .owned = .{
   199	                    .page = page_,
   200	                    .alloc = alloc,
   201	                } };
   202	            },
   203	        };
   204	    }
   205	
   206	    /// Return the node's backing-memory representation without restoring it.
   207	    pub inline fn storage(self: *const Node) Storage {
   208	        return switch (self.data) {
   209	            .resident => .resident,
   210	            .compressed => .compressed,
   211	        };
   212	    }
   213	
   214	    /// Return a page which the caller knows is already resident.
   215	    ///
   216	    /// This avoids the representation check in hot paths which already hold
   217	    /// live pointers into the page mapping. Such pointers are only valid while
   218	    /// the page is resident. Prefer `page` unless the caller can establish
   219	    /// that invariant independently.
   220	    pub inline fn pageAssumeResident(self: *Node) *Page {
   221	        return &self.data.resident;
   222	    }
   223	
   224	    /// Return the number of populated rows without accessing page memory.
   225	    pub inline fn rows(self: *const Node) size.CellCountInt {
   226	        return self.metadata().size.rows;
   227	    }
   228	
   229	    /// Return the current column count without accessing page memory.
   230	    pub inline fn cols(self: *const Node) size.CellCountInt {
   231	        return self.metadata().size.cols;
   232	    }
   233	
   234	    /// Return the page capacity without accessing page memory.
   235	    pub inline fn capacity(self: *const Node) Capacity {
   236	        return self.metadata().capacity;
   237	    }
   238	
   239	    /// Return the embedded Page metadata without restoring its memory.
   240	    inline fn metadata(self: *const Node) *const Page {
   241	        return switch (self.data) {
   242	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   243	            .compressed => |*page_| &page_.page,
   244	        };
   245	    }
   246	
   247	    const RestoreMode = enum {
   248	        /// Decode the compressed representation back into the raw mapping.
   249	        preserve,
   250	
   251	        /// Discard the compressed representation without decoding it. The
   252	        /// caller must not read the page contents before overwriting them.
   253	        discard,
   254	    };
   255	
   256	    /// Restore this node to the resident representation.
   257	    ///
   258	    /// Preserve mode reconstructs the page contents and is used by `page`.
   259	    /// Discard mode skips decoding for callers which will overwrite or destroy
   260	    /// the page. Both modes recommit the retained mapping, free the encoded
   261	    /// allocation, and leave the node in a valid resident state.
   262	    noinline fn restore(self: *Node, comptime mode: RestoreMode) *Page {
   263	        const compressed = switch (self.data) {
   264	            .resident => |*page_| return page_,
   265	            .compressed => |*page_| page_,
   266	        };
   267	
   268	        // Decommit only discarded the physical pages. Recommit prepares the
   269	        // still-reserved mapping for decoding or reuse by the caller.
   270	        terminal_mem.recommit(compressed.page.memory);

   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }

   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},

   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.

   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(
   169	        self: *const Node,
   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {
   175	                const memory = try alloc.alignedAlloc(
   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );

   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {

   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.
   185	                    switch (err) {
   186	                        error.TruncatedInput,
   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
   195	                    @panic("failed to clone compressed terminal page");
   196	                };

   198	                break :owned .{ .owned = .{
   199	                    .page = page_,
   200	                    .alloc = alloc,
   201	                } };
   202	            },
   203	        };
   204	    }

   207	    pub inline fn storage(self: *const Node) Storage {

   209	            .resident => .resident,
   210	            .compressed => .compressed,

   240	    inline fn metadata(self: *const Node) *const Page {
   241	        return switch (self.data) {

   247	    const RestoreMode = enum {
   248	        /// Decode the compressed representation back into the raw mapping.
   249	        preserve,
   250

   252	        /// caller must not read the page contents before overwriting them.

   256	    /// Restore this node to the resident representation.

   258	    /// Preserve mode reconstructs the page contents and is used by `page`.
   259	    /// Discard mode skips decoding for callers which will overwrite or destroy

   261	    /// allocation, and leave the node in a valid resident state.
   262	    noinline fn restore(self: *Node, comptime mode: RestoreMode) *Page {

   264	            .resident => |*page_| return page_,
   265	            .compressed => |*page_| page_,
   266	        };

   268	        // Decommit only discarded the physical pages. Recommit prepares the
   269	        // still-reserved mapping for decoding or reuse by the caller.
   270	        terminal_mem.recommit(compressed.page.memory);

    38	pub fn init(
    39	    io: std.Io,
    40	    alloc: Allocator,
    41	    opts: Screen.Options,
    42	) Allocator.Error!ScreenSet {
    43	    // We need to initialize our initial primary screen
    44	    const screen = try alloc.create(Screen);
    45	    errdefer alloc.destroy(screen);
    46	    screen.* = try .init(io, alloc, opts);
    47	    return .{
    48	        .active_key = .primary,
    49	        .active = screen,
    50	        .all = .init(.{ .primary = screen }),
    51	        .generations = .initFull(0),
    52	    };
    53	}

    55	pub fn deinit(self: *ScreenSet, alloc: Allocator) void {
    56	    // Destroy all initialized screens
    57	    var it = self.all.iterator();
    58	    while (it.next()) |entry| {
    59	        entry.value.*.deinit();
    60	        alloc.destroy(entry.value.*);
    61	    }
    62	}

    64	/// Get the screen for the given key, if it is initialized.

    74	/// Get the screen for the given key, initializing it if necessary.
    75	pub fn getInit(
    76	    self: *ScreenSet,
    77	    io: std.Io,
    78	    alloc: Allocator,
    79	    key: Key,
    80	    opts: Screen.Options,
    81	) Allocator.Error!*Screen {
    82	    if (self.get(key)) |screen| return screen;
    83	    const screen = try alloc.create(Screen);
    84	    errdefer alloc.destroy(screen);
    85	    screen.* = try .init(io, alloc, opts);
    86	    self.all.put(key, screen);
    87	    return screen;
    88	}

    90	/// Remove a key from the set. The primary screen cannot be removed (asserted).
    91	pub fn remove(
    92	    self: *ScreenSet,
    93	    alloc: Allocator,
    94	    key: Key,
    95	) void {
    96	    assert(key != .primary);
    97	    if (self.all.fetchRemove(key)) |screen| {
    98	        self.generations.put(key, self.generation(key) +% 1);
    99	        screen.deinit();

   108	    self.active = self.all.get(key).?;

   117	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.primary));
   118	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));

   131	    var set: ScreenSet = try .init(io, alloc, .default);
   132	    defer set.deinit(alloc);
   133	
   134	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.primary));
   135	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));
   136

   138	    set.remove(alloc, .alternate);
   139	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));
   140	
   141	    // Initializing a screen doesn't change the generation.
   142	    _ = try set.getInit(io, alloc, .alternate, .default);
   143	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));
   144	
   145	    const alternate_generation = set.generation(.alternate);
   146	    set.remove(alloc, .alternate);

   149	    // Reinitializing keeps the generation from the last removal, so stale
   150	    // handles can distinguish the new screen from the destroyed screen.
   151	    _ = try set.getInit(io, alloc, .alternate, .default);
   152	    try testing.expectEqual(alternate_generation +% 1, set.generation(.alternate));

    51	/// The list of pages in the screen. These are expected to be in order
    52	/// where the first page is the topmost page (scrollback) and the last is
    53	/// the bottommost page (the current active page).
    54	pub const List = DoublyLinkedList(Node);

    56	/// A single node within the PageList linked list.
    57	///
    58	/// This isn't pub because you can access the type via List.Node.
    59	const Node = struct {
    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   116	    pub inline fn pageIfResident(self: *Node) ?*Page {
   117	        return switch (self.data) {
   118	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   119	            .compressed => null,
   120	        };
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    /// Read-only page with full memory access that doesn't change
   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains
   125	    /// compressed.
   126	    ///
   127	    /// Resident pages are borrowed directly. So they're basically free.
   128	    ///
   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page
   130	    /// by the caller so callers can inspect their contents. Because resident
   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},
   152	                // The clone buffer came from the caller's allocator rather
   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.
   154	                .owned => |*owned| owned.alloc.free(owned.page.memory),
   155	            }
   156	            self.* = undefined;
   157	        }
   158	    };
   159	
   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(
   169	        self: *const Node,
   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {
   175	                const memory = try alloc.alignedAlloc(
   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );
   180	
   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {
   182	                    // The encoded data was produced by our codec and remains
   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.
   185	                    switch (err) {
   186	                        error.TruncatedInput,
   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
   195	                    @panic("failed to clone compressed terminal page");
   196	                };
   197	
   198	                break :owned .{ .owned = .{
   199	                    .page = page_,
   200	                    .alloc = alloc,
   201	                } };
   202	            },
   203	        };
   204	    }

   206	    /// Return the node's backing-memory representation without restoring it.
   207	    pub inline fn storage(self: *const Node) Storage {
   208	        return switch (self.data) {
   209	            .resident => .resident,
   210	            .compressed => .compressed,
   211	        };
   212	    }

   214	    /// Return a page which the caller knows is already resident.
   215	    ///
   216	    /// This avoids the representation check in hot paths which already hold

   218	    /// the page is resident. Prefer `page` unless the caller can establish
   219	    /// that invariant independently.
   220	    pub inline fn pageAssumeResident(self: *Node) *Page {
   221	        return &self.data.resident;

   226	        return self.metadata().size.rows;

   232	    }

   234	    /// Return the page capacity without accessing page memory.

   236	        return self.metadata().capacity;
   237	    }

   239	    /// Return the embedded Page metadata without restoring its memory.
   240	    inline fn metadata(self: *const Node) *const Page {
   241	        return switch (self.data) {
   242	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   243	            .compressed => |*page_| &page_.page,

   245	    }

   247	    const RestoreMode = enum {
   248	        /// Decode the compressed representation back into the raw mapping.
   249	        preserve,
   250	
   251	        /// Discard the compressed representation without decoding it. The
   252	        /// caller must not read the page contents before overwriting them.

   254	    };

   256	    /// Restore this node to the resident representation.

   261	    /// allocation, and leave the node in a valid resident state.
   262	    noinline fn restore(self: *Node, comptime mode: RestoreMode) *Page {
   263	        const compressed = switch (self.data) {
   264	            .resident => |*page_| return page_,
   265	            .compressed => |*page_| page_,
   266	        };
   267	
   268	        // Decommit only discarded the physical pages. Recommit prepares the
   269	        // still-reserved mapping for decoding or reuse by the caller.
   270	        terminal_mem.recommit(compressed.page.memory);

     1	//! Maintains a linked list of pages to make up a terminal screen
     2	//! and provides higher level operations on top of those pages to
     3	//! make it slightly easier to work with.

     5	
     6	const std = @import("std");

    33	    !builtin.target.cpu.arch.isWasm();
    34	
    35	/// The number of pages we preheat the page pool with. For operating systems
    36	/// that support it, pages are demand-paged (see PagePool) so this only
    37	/// costs us address space. For other operating systems, we don't preheat.
    38	const page_preheat = 4;
    39	
    40	/// The number of nodes we preheat the node pool with. Unlike pages, nodes
    41	/// are ordinary heap memory so every idle preheated node costs real
    42	/// memory. A new PageList needs exactly one node for its first page, so
    43	/// we preheat that one and let the pool grow on demand.
    44	const node_preheat = 1;
    45	
    46	/// The number of pins we preheat the pin pool with: the viewport pin that
    47	/// every PageList tracks and the cursor pin that every Screen tracks.
    48	/// Selections, searches, and so on grow the pool on demand.
    49	const pin_preheat = 2;
    50	
    51	/// The list of pages in the screen. These are expected to be in order
    52	/// where the first page is the topmost page (scrollback) and the last is
    53	/// the bottommost page (the current active page).
    54	pub const List = DoublyLinkedList(Node);
    55	
    56	/// A single node within the PageList linked list.
    57	///
    58	/// This isn't pub because you can access the type via List.Node.
    59	const Node = struct {
    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   116	    pub inline fn pageIfResident(self: *Node) ?*Page {
   117	        return switch (self.data) {
   118	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   119	            .compressed => null,
   120	        };
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    /// Read-only page with full memory access that doesn't change
   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains
   125	    /// compressed.
   126	    ///
   127	    /// Resident pages are borrowed directly. So they're basically free.
   128	    ///
   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page
   130	    /// by the caller so callers can inspect their contents. Because resident
   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},
   152	                // The clone buffer came from the caller's allocator rather
   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.
   154	                .owned => |*owned| owned.alloc.free(owned.page.memory),
   155	            }
   156	            self.* = undefined;
   157	        }
   158	    };
   159	
   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(
   169	        self: *const Node,
   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {
   175	                const memory = try alloc.alignedAlloc(
   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );
   180	
   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {
   182	                    // The encoded data was produced by our codec and remains
   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.
   185	                    switch (err) {
   186	                        error.TruncatedInput,
   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
   195	                    @panic("failed to clone compressed terminal page");
   196	                };
   197	
   198	                break :owned .{ .owned = .{
   199	                    .page = page_,
   200	                    .alloc = alloc,
   201	                } };
   202	            },
   203	        };
   204	    }
   205	
   206	    /// Return the node's backing-memory representation without restoring it.
   207	    pub inline fn storage(self: *const Node) Storage {
   208	        return switch (self.data) {
   209	            .resident => .resident,
   210	            .compressed => .compressed,
   211	        };
   212	    }
   213	
   214	    /// Return a page which the caller knows is already resident.
   215	    ///
   216	    /// This avoids the representation check in hot paths which already hold
   217	    /// live pointers into the page mapping. Such pointers are only valid while
   218	    /// the page is resident. Prefer `page` unless the caller can establish
   219	    /// that invariant independently.
   220	    pub inline fn pageAssumeResident(self: *Node) *Page {
   221	        return &self.data.resident;
   222	    }
   223	
   224	    /// Return the number of populated rows without accessing page memory.
   225	    pub inline fn rows(self: *const Node) size.CellCountInt {
   226	        return self.metadata().size.rows;
   227	    }
   228	
   229	    /// Return the current column count without accessing page memory.
   230	    pub inline fn cols(self: *const Node) size.CellCountInt {
   231	        return self.metadata().size.cols;
   232	    }
   233	
   234	    /// Return the page capacity without accessing page memory.
   235	    pub inline fn capacity(self: *const Node) Capacity {
   236	        return self.metadata().capacity;
   237	    }
   238	
   239	    /// Return the embedded Page metadata without restoring its memory.
   240	    inline fn metadata(self: *const Node) *const Page {
   241	        return switch (self.data) {
   242	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   243	            .compressed => |*page_| &page_.page,
   244	        };
   245	    }
   246	
   247	    const RestoreMode = enum {
   248	        /// Decode the compressed representation back into the raw mapping.
   249	        preserve,
   250	
   251	        /// Discard the compressed representation without decoding it. The
   252	        /// caller must not read the page contents before overwriting them.
   253	        discard,
   254	    };
   255	
   256	    /// Restore this node to the resident representation.
   257	    ///
   258	    /// Preserve mode reconstructs the page contents and is used by `page`.
   259	    /// Discard mode skips decoding for callers which will overwrite or destroy
   260	    /// the page. Both modes recommit the retained mapping, free the encoded
   261	    /// allocation, and leave the node in a valid resident state.
   262	    noinline fn restore(self: *Node, comptime mode: RestoreMode) *Page {
   263	        const compressed = switch (self.data) {
   264	            .resident => |*page_| return page_,
   265	            .compressed => |*page_| page_,
   266	        };
   267	
   268	        // Decommit only discarded the physical pages. Recommit prepares the
   269	        // still-reserved mapping for decoding or reuse by the caller.
   270	        terminal_mem.recommit(compressed.page.memory);

   309	/// The memory pool we get page nodes from.
   310	///
   311	/// We don't use a std memory pool here because it is backed by an arena
   312	/// and we end up paying a lot of wasted memory for the growth factor when
   313	/// in practice we don't usually use many nodes.
   314	///
   315	/// We don't need the "untouched" property of our UntouchedPool but
   316	/// this gives us a GPA-allocated pool so we reuse it here.
   317	const NodePool = datastruct.UntouchedPool(List.Node, .of(List.Node));
   318	
   319	/// The standard page capacity that we use as a starting point for
   320	/// all pages. This is chosen as a sane default that fits most terminal
   321	/// usage to support using our pool.
   322	const std_capacity = pagepkg.std_capacity;
   323	
   324	/// The byte size required for a standard page.
   325	const std_size = Page.layout(std_capacity).total_size;
   326	
   327	/// True when the page pool is the wasm page pool, which recycles items
   328	/// through a free list shared by the whole module instance instead of
   329	/// dying with the pool.
   330	///
   331	/// Test builds use the native pool even on wasm so that pool memory goes
   332	/// through the testing allocator and participates in leak detection.
   333	const wasm_page_pool = builtin.target.cpu.arch.isWasm() and !builtin.is_test;
   334	
   335	/// The memory pool we use for page memory buffers. We use a separate pool
   336	/// so we can allocate these with a page allocator. We have to use a page
   337	/// allocator because we need memory that is zero-initialized and page-aligned.
   338	const PagePool = if (wasm_page_pool)
   339	    datastruct.WasmPagePool([std_size]u8)
   340	else untouched: {
   341	    // Untouched pools never read/write to the items so that we can
   342	    // use demand-paging on operating systems that support it. This makes
   343	    // it so that an idle item in the pool costs no physical memory,
   344	    // only virtual memory.
   345	    //
   346	    // Contract for PageList is that every path that returns an item
   347	    // to the pool must zero it.
   348	    break :untouched datastruct.UntouchedPool(
   349	        [std_size]u8,
   350	        .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   351	    );
   352	};
   353	
   354	/// List of pins, known as "tracked" pins. These are pins that are kept
   355	/// up to date automatically through page-modifying operations.
   356	const PinSet = std.AutoArrayHashMapUnmanaged(*Pin, void);
   357	const PinPool = std.heap.MemoryPool(Pin);
   358	
   359	/// The pool of memory used for a pagelist. This can be shared between
   360	/// multiple pagelists but it is not threadsafe.
   361	pub const MemoryPool = struct {
   362	    alloc: Allocator,
   363	    nodes: NodePool,
   364	    pages: PagePool,
   365	    pins: PinPool,
   366	
   367	    pub const ResetMode = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.ResetMode;
   368	
   369	    pub fn init(
   370	        gen_alloc: Allocator,
   371	        page_alloc: Allocator,
   372	        preheat: usize,
   373	    ) Allocator.Error!MemoryPool {
   374	        var node_pool = try NodePool.initCapacity(gen_alloc, gen_alloc, node_preheat);
   375	        errdefer node_pool.deinit();
   376	        var page_pool = try PagePool.initCapacity(gen_alloc, page_alloc, preheat);
   377	        errdefer page_pool.deinit();
   378	        var pin_pool = try PinPool.initCapacity(gen_alloc, pin_preheat);
   379	        errdefer pin_pool.deinit();
   380	        return .{
   381	            .alloc = gen_alloc,
   382	            .nodes = node_pool,
   383	            .pages = page_pool,
   384	            .pins = pin_pool,
   385	        };
   386	    }

   388	    pub fn deinit(self: *MemoryPool) void {
   389	        self.pages.deinit();
   390	        self.nodes.deinit();
   391	        self.pins.deinit(self.alloc);
   392	    }
   393	
   394	    pub fn reset(self: *MemoryPool, mode: ResetMode) void {
   395	        _ = self.pages.reset(mode);
   396	        _ = self.nodes.reset(mode);
   397	        _ = self.pins.reset(mode);
   398	    }
   399	};

   401	/// The memory pool we get page nodes, pages from.
   402	pool: MemoryPool,
   403	
   404	/// The list of pages in the screen.
   405	pages: List,
   406	
   407	/// The next globally unique reference generation for this PageList. A
   408	/// generation is assigned whenever a page is allocated, reused as new, or
   409	/// changed in place such that existing page coordinates are no longer stable.
   410	///
   411	/// The serial number can be used to detect whether the page is identical
   412	/// to the page that was originally referenced by a pointer. Since we reuse
   413	/// and pool memory, pointer stability is not guaranteed, but the serial
   414	/// will always be different for different page generations.
   415	///
   416	/// Developer note: we never do overflow checking on this. If we created
   417	/// a new page every second it'd take 584 billion years to overflow. We're
   418	/// going to risk it.
   419	page_serial: u64,
   420	
   421	/// The first serial in the current whole-list validity epoch. Only `reset`
   422	/// advances this value, immediately before rebuilding every page. It is not
   423	/// the generation of the first page or the exact minimum live generation.
   424	/// Page generations are not monotonic in list order: replacement and split
   425	/// operations can put a fresh generation before older live pages.
   426	///
   427	/// A generation below this epoch is definitely invalid, allowing O(1)
   428	/// rejection in `nodeIsValid` and bulk removal of pre-reset search results.
   429	/// A generation at or above it is only potentially valid and must still be
   430	/// checked against the live list before its coordinates are used.
   431	page_serial_epoch: u64,
   432	
   433	/// Byte size of the raw backing mappings owned by active page nodes. This is
   434	/// logical scrollback accounting and does not change while a mapping is
   435	/// decommitted. It excludes encoded storage and unused preheated pool items.
   436	page_size: usize,
   437	
   438	/// Continuation state for incremental page compression. This allows
   439	/// compress(.incremental) to work. More details on all that there and
   440	/// in the state struct.
   441	page_compression: IncrementalCompressionState = .{},
   442	
   443	/// A node available for immediate reuse by createPage, bypassing the
   444	/// memory pool round trip. This is only set during column reflow
   445	/// (resizeCols), which destroys one source page for roughly every
   446	/// destination page it creates: returning a page buffer to the pool
   447	/// decommits it and taking one back recommits it, and that syscall
   448	/// pair per page is a significant part of reflow cost. Always null
   449	/// outside of an in-progress reflow.
   450	recycle_node: ?*List.Node = null,
   451	
   452	/// The capacities that the last `grow_hint_pages` full pages before the
   453	/// last one needed for styles, graphemes, strings, and hyperlinks,
   454	/// measured by `utilizationCapacity` when `grow` moved past each of
   455	/// them. `grow` gives each new page the largest of these and what the
   456	/// page that just filled needed, so a new page reflects the last few
   457	/// full pages instead of only the last one. See `growCapacity` for why.
   458	///
   459	/// This is a ring: `grow_hint_next` is the slot the next need goes in.
   460	/// Slots are null until that many pages have filled up, and `reset`
   461	/// clears them. `growHint` combines them.
   462	grow_hints: [grow_hint_pages]?GrowHint = @splat(null),
   463	grow_hint_next: usize = 0,
   464	
   465	/// Limits for scrollback.
   466	limits: Limits,
   467	
   468	/// The total number of rows represented by this PageList. This is used
   469	/// specifically for scrollbar information so we can have the total size.
   470	total_rows: usize,
   471	
   472	/// The list of tracked pins. These are kept up to date automatically.
   473	tracked_pins: PinSet,
   474	
   475	/// The top-left of certain parts of the screen that are frequently
   476	/// accessed so we don't have to traverse the linked list to find them.
   477	///
   478	/// For other tags, don't need this:
   479	///   - screen: pages.first
   480	///   - history: active row minus one
   481	///
   482	viewport: Viewport,
   483	
   484	/// The pin used for when the viewport scrolls. This is always pre-allocated
   485	/// so that scrolling doesn't have a failable memory allocation. This should
   486	/// never be access directly; use `viewport`.
   487	viewport_pin: *Pin,
   488	
   489	/// The row offset from the top that the viewport pin is at. We
   490	/// store the offset from the top because it doesn't change while more
   491	/// data is printed to the terminal.
   492	///
   493	/// This is null when it isn't calculated. It is calculated on demand
   494	/// when the viewportRowOffset function is called, because it is only
   495	/// required for certain operations such as rendering the scrollbar.
   496	///
   497	/// In order to make this more efficient, in many places where the value
   498	/// would be invalidated, we update it in-place instead. This is key to
   499	/// keeping our performance decent in normal cases since recalculating
   500	/// this from scratch, depending on the size of the scrollback and position
   501	/// of the pin, can be very expensive.
   502	///
   503	/// This is only valid if viewport is `pin`. Every other offset is
   504	/// self-evident or quick to calculate.
   505	viewport_pin_row_offset: ?usize,
   506	
   507	/// The current desired screen dimensions. I say "desired" because individual
   508	/// pages may still be a different size and not yet reflowed since we lazily
   509	/// reflow text.
   510	cols: size.CellCountInt,
   511	rows: size.CellCountInt,
   512	
   513	/// If this is true then verifyIntegrity will do nothing. This is
   514	/// only present with runtime safety enabled.
   515	pause_integrity_checks: if (build_options.slow_runtime_safety) usize else void =
   516	    if (build_options.slow_runtime_safety) 0 else {},
   517	
   518	/// The viewport location.
   519	pub const Viewport = union(enum) {
   520	    /// The viewport is pinned to the active area. By using a specific marker
   521	    /// for this instead of tracking the row offset, we eliminate a number of
   522	    /// memory writes making scrolling faster.
   523	    active,
   524	
   525	    /// The viewport is pinned to the top of the screen, or the farthest
   526	    /// back in the scrollback history.
   527	    top,
   528	
   529	    /// The viewport is pinned to a tracked pin. The tracked pin is ALWAYS
   530	    /// s.viewport_pin hence this has no value. We force that value to prevent
   531	    /// allocations.
   532	    pin,
   533	};
   534	
   535	/// Calculates the initial capacity for a new page for a given column
   536	/// count. This will attempt to fit within std_size at all times so we
   537	/// can use our memory pool, but if cols is too big, this will return a
   538	/// larger capacity.
   539	///
   540	/// The returned capacity is always guaranteed to layout properly (not
   541	/// overflow). We are able to support capacities up to the maximum int
   542	/// value of cols, so this will never overflow.
   543	fn initialCapacity(cols: size.CellCountInt) Capacity {
   544	    // This is an important invariant that ensures that this function
   545	    // can never return an error. We verify here that our standard capacity
   546	    // when increased to maximum possible columns can always support at
   547	    // least one row in memory.
   548	    //
   549	    // IF THIS EVER FAILS: We probably need to modify our logic below
   550	    // to reduce other elements of the capacity (styles, graphemes, etc.).
   551	    // But, instead, I recommend taking a step back and re-evaluating
   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {
   554	        var cap = std_capacity;
   555	        cap.cols = std.math.maxInt(size.CellCountInt);
   556	        const layout = Page.layout(cap);
   557	        assert(layout.total_size <= size.max_page_size);
   558	    }
   559	
   560	    if (std_capacity.adjust(
   561	        .{ .cols = cols },
   562	    )) |cap| {
   563	        // If we can adjust our standard capacity, we fit within the
   564	        // standard size and we're good!
   565	        return cap;
   566	    } else |err| {
   567	        // Ensure our error set doesn't change.
   568	        comptime assert(@TypeOf(err) == error{OutOfMemory});
   569	    }
   570	
   571	    // This code path means that our standard capacity can't even
   572	    // accommodate our column count! The only solution is to increase
   573	    // our capacity and go non-standard.
   574	    var cap: Capacity = std_capacity;
   575	    cap.cols = cols;
   576	    return cap;
   577	}
   578	
   579	/// Returns the allocator used for underlying page allocations.
   580	///
   581	/// `alloc` is the caller-provided allocator. It is used on native freestanding
   582	/// targets, where no OS page allocator is available. Other targets select a
   583	/// platform-specific allocator below.
   584	inline fn pageAllocator(alloc: Allocator) Allocator {
   585	    // In tests we use our testing allocator so we can detect leaks.
   586	    if (builtin.is_test) return std.testing.allocator;
   587	
   588	    // Native freestanding targets don't have an OS page allocator, so use
   589	    // the allocator provided by the embedder.
   590	    if (native_freestanding) return alloc;
   591	
   592	    // On non-macOS we use our standard Zig page allocator.
   593	    if (!builtin.target.os.tag.isDarwin()) return std.heap.page_allocator;
   594	
   595	    // On macOS we want to tag our memory so we can assign it to our
   596	    // core terminal usage.
   597	    const mach = @import("../os/mach.zig");
   598	    return mach.taggedPageAllocator(.application_specific_1);
   599	}
   600	
   601	const init_tw = tripwire.module(enum {
   602	    init_memory_pool,
   603	    init_pages,
   604	    viewport_pin,
   605	    viewport_pin_track,
   606	}, init);
   607	
   608	pub const Options = struct {
   609	    /// The initial active-area size. This can be resized with `resize`.
   610	    cols: size.CellCountInt,
   611	    rows: size.CellCountInt,
   612	
   613	    /// The maximum number of bytes allocated for pages. The effective limit
   614	    /// is raised when necessary to hold the active area. Null is unlimited.
   615	    max_size: ?usize = null,
   616	
   617	    /// The maximum number of scrollback rows, excluding the active
   618	    /// area. Rows are physical (viewed) rows, so a wrapped row counts as
   619	    /// multiple rows. Max line pruning only happens at page-boundaries
   620	    /// (the minimum internal allocation size) so in practice the max lines
   621	    /// is always slightly larger than configured.
   622	    ///
   623	    /// Null is unlimited.
   624	    max_lines: ?usize = null,
   625	};
   626	
   627	/// Initialize the page. The top of the first page in the list is always the
   628	/// top of the active area of the screen (important knowledge for quickly
   629	/// setting up cursors in Screen).
   630	///
   631	/// `max_size` is the maximum number of bytes that will be allocated for
   632	/// pages. If this is smaller than the bytes required to show the viewport
   633	/// then max_size will be ignored and the viewport will be shown, but no
   634	/// scrollback will be created. max_size is always rounded down to the nearest
   635	/// terminal page size (not virtual memory page), otherwise we would always
   636	/// slightly exceed max_size in the limits.
   637	///
   638	/// `max_lines` is the maximum number of physical rows retained as scrollback,
   639	/// excluding the active area. It is a page-granular heuristic: at least one
   640	/// standard page worth of rows is permitted and only complete historical
   641	/// pages are removed.
   642	///
   643	/// If either limit is null then that dimension has no defined limit and the
   644	/// screen will grow forever. In reality, the limit is set to the amount your
   645	/// computer can address in memory. If you somehow require more than that (due
   646	/// to disk paging) then please contribute that yourself and perhaps search
   647	/// deep within yourself to find out why you need that.
   648	pub fn init(
   649	    alloc: Allocator,
   650	    opts: Options,
   651	) Allocator.Error!PageList {
   652	    const tw = init_tw;
   653	    const cols = opts.cols;
   654	    const rows = opts.rows;
   655	
   656	    // The screen starts with a single page that is the entire viewport,
   657	    // and we'll split it thereafter if it gets too large and add more as
   658	    // necessary.
   659	    try tw.check(.init_memory_pool);
   660	    var pool = try MemoryPool.init(
   661	        alloc,
   662	        pageAllocator(alloc),
   663	        page_preheat,
   664	    );
   665	    errdefer pool.deinit();
   666	
   667	    try tw.check(.init_pages);
   668	    var page_serial: u64 = 0;
   669	    const page_list, const page_size = try initPages(
   670	        &pool,
   671	        &page_serial,
   672	        cols,
   673	        rows,
   674	    );
   675	    errdefer releasePages(&pool, page_list);
   676	
   677	    var limits: Limits = .init(cols, rows);
   678	    limits.set(.bytes, opts.max_size);
   679	    limits.set(.lines, opts.max_lines);
   680	
   681	    // We always track our viewport pin to ensure this is never an allocation
   682	    try tw.check(.viewport_pin);
   683	    const viewport_pin = try pool.pins.create(pool.alloc);
   684	    viewport_pin.* = .{ .node = page_list.first.? };

   548	    //

   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {

   535	/// Calculates the initial capacity for a new page for a given column
   536	/// count. This will attempt to fit within std_size at all times so we
   537	/// can use our memory pool, but if cols is too big, this will return a
   538	/// larger capacity.
   539	///
   540	/// The returned capacity is always guaranteed to layout properly (not
   541	/// overflow). We are able to support capacities up to the maximum int
   542	/// value of cols, so this will never overflow.
   543	fn initialCapacity(cols: size.CellCountInt) Capacity {
   544	    // This is an important invariant that ensures that this function
   545	    // can never return an error. We verify here that our standard capacity
   546	    // when increased to maximum possible columns can always support at
   547	    // least one row in memory.
   548	    //
   549	    // IF THIS EVER FAILS: We probably need to modify our logic below
   550	    // to reduce other elements of the capacity (styles, graphemes, etc.).
   551	    // But, instead, I recommend taking a step back and re-evaluating
   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {
   554	        var cap = std_capacity;
   555	        cap.cols = std.math.maxInt(size.CellCountInt);
   556	        const layout = Page.layout(cap);
   557	        assert(layout.total_size <= size.max_page_size);
   558	    }
   559	
   560	    if (std_capacity.adjust(
   561	        .{ .cols = cols },
   562	    )) |cap| {
   563	        // If we can adjust our standard capacity, we fit within the
   564	        // standard size and we're good!
   565	        return cap;
   566	    } else |err| {
   567	        // Ensure our error set doesn't change.
   568	        comptime assert(@TypeOf(err) == error{OutOfMemory});
   569	    }
   570	
   571	    // This code path means that our standard capacity can't even
   572	    // accommodate our column count! The only solution is to increase
   573	    // our capacity and go non-standard.
   574	    var cap: Capacity = std_capacity;
   575	    cap.cols = cols;
   576	    return cap;
   577	}

Map each node in every diagram on the provided canvas to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change any diagram’s text or the canvas layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (terminal):
Map d5 all nodes. Read numbered source ranges, return JSON partial mappings.

     1	/// A ScreenSet holds multiple terminal screens. This is initially created
     2	/// to handle simple primary vs alternate screens, but could be extended
     3	/// in the future to handle N screens.
     4	///
     5	/// One of the goals of this is to allow lazy initialization of screens
     6	/// as needed. The primary screen is always initialized, but the alternate
     7	/// screen may not be until first used.
     8	const ScreenSet = @This();
     9	
    10	const std = @import("std");
    11	const assert = @import("../quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    12	const lib = @import("lib.zig");
    13	const testing = std.testing;
    14	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;

    16	
    17	/// The possible keys for screens in the screen set.
    18	pub const Key = lib.Enum(lib.target, &.{
    19	    "primary",
    20	    "alternate",
    21	});
    22	
    23	/// The key value of the currently active screen. Useful for simple
    24	/// comparisons, e.g. "is this screen the primary screen".
    25	active_key: Key,
    26	
    27	/// The active screen pointer.
    28	active: *Screen,
    29	
    30	/// All screens that are initialized.
    31	all: std.EnumMap(Key, *Screen),
    32	
    33	/// Monotonic generation counter for each screen key. This changes whenever
    34	/// screen storage is removed or replaced so external handles can distinguish a
    35	/// newly initialized screen from stale references into destroyed storage.
    36	generations: std.EnumMap(Key, usize),
    37	
    38	pub fn init(
    39	    io: std.Io,
    40	    alloc: Allocator,
    41	    opts: Screen.Options,
    42	) Allocator.Error!ScreenSet {
    43	    // We need to initialize our initial primary screen
    44	    const screen = try alloc.create(Screen);
    45	    errdefer alloc.destroy(screen);
    46	    screen.* = try .init(io, alloc, opts);
    47	    return .{
    48	        .active_key = .primary,
    49	        .active = screen,
    50	        .all = .init(.{ .primary = screen }),
    51	        .generations = .initFull(0),
    52	    };
    53	}
    54	
    55	pub fn deinit(self: *ScreenSet, alloc: Allocator) void {
    56	    // Destroy all initialized screens
    57	    var it = self.all.iterator();
    58	    while (it.next()) |entry| {
    59	        entry.value.*.deinit();
    60	        alloc.destroy(entry.value.*);
    61	    }
    62	}
    63	
    64	/// Get the screen for the given key, if it is initialized.
    65	pub fn get(self: *const ScreenSet, key: Key) ?*Screen {
    66	    return self.all.get(key);
    67	}
    68	
    69	/// Get the current generation for the given screen key.
    70	pub fn generation(self: *const ScreenSet, key: Key) usize {
    71	    return self.generations.get(key).?;
    72	}
    73	
    74	/// Get the screen for the given key, initializing it if necessary.
    75	pub fn getInit(
    76	    self: *ScreenSet,
    77	    io: std.Io,
    78	    alloc: Allocator,
    79	    key: Key,
    80	    opts: Screen.Options,
    81	) Allocator.Error!*Screen {
    82	    if (self.get(key)) |screen| return screen;
    83	    const screen = try alloc.create(Screen);
    84	    errdefer alloc.destroy(screen);
    85	    screen.* = try .init(io, alloc, opts);
    86	    self.all.put(key, screen);
    87	    return screen;
    88	}
    89	
    90	/// Remove a key from the set. The primary screen cannot be removed (asserted).
    91	pub fn remove(
    92	    self: *ScreenSet,
    93	    alloc: Allocator,
    94	    key: Key,
    95	) void {
    96	    assert(key != .primary);
    97	    if (self.all.fetchRemove(key)) |screen| {
    98	        self.generations.put(key, self.generation(key) +% 1);
    99	        screen.deinit();
   100	        alloc.destroy(screen);
   101	    }
   102	}
   103	
   104	/// Switch the active screen to the given key. Requires that the
   105	/// screen is initialized.
   106	pub fn switchTo(self: *ScreenSet, key: Key) void {
   107	    self.active_key = key;
   108	    self.active = self.all.get(key).?;
   109	}

   111	test ScreenSet {
   112	    const alloc = testing.allocator;
   113	    const io = testing.io;
   114	    var set: ScreenSet = try .init(io, alloc, .default);
   115	    defer set.deinit(alloc);
   116	    try testing.expectEqual(.primary, set.active_key);
   117	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.primary));
   118	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));
   119	
   120	    // Initialize a secondary screen
   121	    _ = try set.getInit(io, alloc, .alternate, .default);
   122	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));
   123	
   124	    set.switchTo(.alternate);
   125	    try testing.expectEqual(.alternate, set.active_key);
   126	}
   127	
   128	test "ScreenSet generations" {
   129	    const alloc = testing.allocator;
   130	    const io = testing.io;
   131	    var set: ScreenSet = try .init(io, alloc, .default);
   132	    defer set.deinit(alloc);
   133	
   134	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.primary));
   135	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));
   136	
   137	    // A no-op removal doesn't change the generation.
   138	    set.remove(alloc, .alternate);
   139	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));
   140	
   141	    // Initializing a screen doesn't change the generation.
   142	    _ = try set.getInit(io, alloc, .alternate, .default);
   143	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.alternate));
   144	
   145	    const alternate_generation = set.generation(.alternate);
   146	    set.remove(alloc, .alternate);
   147	    try testing.expectEqual(alternate_generation +% 1, set.generation(.alternate));
   148	
   149	    // Reinitializing keeps the generation from the last removal, so stale
   150	    // handles can distinguish the new screen from the destroyed screen.
   151	    _ = try set.getInit(io, alloc, .alternate, .default);
   152	    try testing.expectEqual(alternate_generation +% 1, set.generation(.alternate));
   153	    try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 0), set.generation(.primary));
   154	}

    35	/// The number of pages we preheat the page pool with. For operating systems
    36	/// that support it, pages are demand-paged (see PagePool) so this only
    37	/// costs us address space. For other operating systems, we don't preheat.
    38	const page_preheat = 4;
    39	
    40	/// The number of nodes we preheat the node pool with. Unlike pages, nodes
    41	/// are ordinary heap memory so every idle preheated node costs real
    42	/// memory. A new PageList needs exactly one node for its first page, so
    43	/// we preheat that one and let the pool grow on demand.
    44	const node_preheat = 1;

    46	/// The number of pins we preheat the pin pool with: the viewport pin that
    47	/// every PageList tracks and the cursor pin that every Screen tracks.
    48	/// Selections, searches, and so on grow the pool on demand.

    51	/// The list of pages in the screen. These are expected to be in order
    52	/// where the first page is the topmost page (scrollback) and the last is
    53	/// the bottommost page (the current active page).
    54	pub const List = DoublyLinkedList(Node);
    55	
    56	/// A single node within the PageList linked list.
    57	///
    58	/// This isn't pub because you can access the type via List.Node.
    59	const Node = struct {
    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   116	    pub inline fn pageIfResident(self: *Node) ?*Page {
   117	        return switch (self.data) {
   118	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   119	            .compressed => null,
   120	        };
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    /// Read-only page with full memory access that doesn't change
   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains
   125	    /// compressed.
   126	    ///
   127	    /// Resident pages are borrowed directly. So they're basically free.
   128	    ///
   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page
   130	    /// by the caller so callers can inspect their contents. Because resident
   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},
   152	                // The clone buffer came from the caller's allocator rather
   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.
   154	                .owned => |*owned| owned.alloc.free(owned.page.memory),
   155	            }
   156	            self.* = undefined;
   157	        }
   158	    };

   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(
   169	        self: *const Node,
   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {
   175	                const memory = try alloc.alignedAlloc(
   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );
   180	
   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {
   182	                    // The encoded data was produced by our codec and remains
   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.
   185	                    switch (err) {
   186	                        error.TruncatedInput,
   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
   195	                    @panic("failed to clone compressed terminal page");
   196	                };
   197	
   198	                break :owned .{ .owned = .{
   199	                    .page = page_,
   200	                    .alloc = alloc,
   201	                } };
   202	            },
   203	        };
   204	    }
   205	
   206	    /// Return the node's backing-memory representation without restoring it.
   207	    pub inline fn storage(self: *const Node) Storage {
   208	        return switch (self.data) {
   209	            .resident => .resident,
   210	            .compressed => .compressed,
   211	        };
   212	    }
   213	
   214	    /// Return a page which the caller knows is already resident.
   215	    ///
   216	    /// This avoids the representation check in hot paths which already hold
   217	    /// live pointers into the page mapping. Such pointers are only valid while
   218	    /// the page is resident. Prefer `page` unless the caller can establish
   219	    /// that invariant independently.
   220	    pub inline fn pageAssumeResident(self: *Node) *Page {
   221	        return &self.data.resident;
   222	    }
   223	
   224	    /// Return the number of populated rows without accessing page memory.
   225	    pub inline fn rows(self: *const Node) size.CellCountInt {
   226	        return self.metadata().size.rows;
   227	    }
   228	
   229	    /// Return the current column count without accessing page memory.
   230	    pub inline fn cols(self: *const Node) size.CellCountInt {
   231	        return self.metadata().size.cols;
   232	    }
   233	
   234	    /// Return the page capacity without accessing page memory.
   235	    pub inline fn capacity(self: *const Node) Capacity {
   236	        return self.metadata().capacity;
   237	    }
   238	
   239	    /// Return the embedded Page metadata without restoring its memory.
   240	    inline fn metadata(self: *const Node) *const Page {
   241	        return switch (self.data) {
   242	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   243	            .compressed => |*page_| &page_.page,
   244	        };
   245	    }
   246	
   247	    const RestoreMode = enum {
   248	        /// Decode the compressed representation back into the raw mapping.
   249	        preserve,
   250	
   251	        /// Discard the compressed representation without decoding it. The
   252	        /// caller must not read the page contents before overwriting them.
   253	        discard,
   254	    };
   255	
   256	    /// Restore this node to the resident representation.
   257	    ///
   258	    /// Preserve mode reconstructs the page contents and is used by `page`.
   259	    /// Discard mode skips decoding for callers which will overwrite or destroy
   260	    /// the page. Both modes recommit the retained mapping, free the encoded
   261	    /// allocation, and leave the node in a valid resident state.
   262	    noinline fn restore(self: *Node, comptime mode: RestoreMode) *Page {
   263	        const compressed = switch (self.data) {
   264	            .resident => |*page_| return page_,
   265	            .compressed => |*page_| page_,
   266	        };
   267	
   268	        // Decommit only discarded the physical pages. Recommit prepares the
   269	        // still-reserved mapping for decoding or reuse by the caller.
   270	        terminal_mem.recommit(compressed.page.memory);
